title: doctor never verifies the MCP client registration that IS the delivery model
description: install merges the server entry into ~/.claude.json, ~/.codex/config.toml and OpenCode's config (install.go:770-797) and configureClients returns which it touched - nothing ever re-reads them. Manager.Status (install.go:378-418) covers only service, definition and updater. Clients rewrite their own configs; when one drops the entry the daemon is healthy, doctor is all green, and Blackbird has simply vanished from the agent's tool list with no diagnostic anywhere. FIX: a clients check group that re-reads each detected config, confirms a blackbird entry pointing at the current mcpURL, and reports configured/drifted/missing with remedy 'run blackbird install'.

title: authorize is cc 93 / cognitive 72 at 0.0 percent coverage
description: localsecurity/security.go:300. The single most complex function in the codebase is the authorization decision and it is entirely untested - AuthorizeLocked, authorize, intersectCapabilities, sameAggregateRefs, NewReplayAuthorization and AuthorizeReplay are all 0.0 percent while the package sits at 67 percent, so this is a hole not a missing file. Shape: a state-projection type-switch loop, then a wall of boolean conjunctions where every failure returns the same bare ErrAccessDenied. FIX: characterization tests FIRST (any refactor is unverifiable without them), then split into named predicates each returning a typed denial reason - which also fixes the undiagnosable-denial problem.

title: The migration ladder has one hardcoded rung; a skipped version dead-ends permanently
description: sqlite.go:298-310 handles exactly three cases: empty DB apply all; schemaVersion == SchemaVersion-1 apply the last migration; anything else ErrSchemaMismatch. The N-1 rung is hardcoded against schemaV3ChecksumHex (:40, used :316), so the NEXT schema bump necessarily deletes the v3->v4 path. Downgrade is correctly fail-closed, but a user offline across two releases (plausible - Homebrew auto-updates every 6h so a shelved laptop skips versions) hits ErrSchemaMismatch permanently, and doctor.go:286 tells them to run blackbird update, which cannot help, with no backup to fall back on. FIX: loop over migrationIDs from the DB's user_version forward so any older-but-known schema converges; split the doctor remedy by direction; take a Backup before applyIncrementalMigration once backup is wired.

title: Backup and Restore are fully implemented, tested, and have zero callers
description: internal/storage/sqlite/backup.go is 588 lines implementing the SQLite online backup API (:193,:225), full integrity_check + foreign_key_check (:311), SHA-256 manifest (:277), hash-chain contiguity (:347), atomic publish with parent-dir fsync (:485), and Restore (:124) with adversarial tests for truncation, corruption, tampered manifests and mid-copy WAL races. Non-test callers: ZERO. No backup or restore command exists (cli.go:39-59), no scheduler, and the backup_sessions table (0001:583) is never written. Meanwhile doctor.go:299 tells the operator to 'stop the daemon and restore the most recent backup'. Structural gap even for a willing caller: BackupManifest (backup.go:35) has no JSON tags and is never serialized, yet Restore requires it and VerifyBackup rejects an incomplete one - so a snapshot on disk with no companion manifest is unrestorable. FIX: blackbird backup/restore commands, manifest as sidecar JSON, install schedules a daily backup like it schedules the updater. Note validateFreshTarget (:446) refuses overwrite and failed snapshots retain .partial.<hex> files (:471) with nothing to reap them, so rotation is part of the wiring.

title: blackbird logs is silently empty on Linux and three doctor remedies point there
description: The launchd plist sets StandardOutPath/StandardErrorPath (install.go:1105-1106). The systemd unit (install.go:1117-1129) sets NEITHER - output goes to the journal. logsource.go:23-24,158-163 only ever reads STATE/blackbird.log and blackbird.err.log, and tailFile treats a missing file as not-an-error (:171). A Linux user gets 'No log lines yet.' Worse: doctor.go:179, :237 and :286 all tell them to run blackbird logs --stream=err. FIX: add StandardOutput=append:%s / StandardError=append:%s to the systemd unit (makes both platforms identical) or add a journald LogPort.

title: Transport logs nothing; the request_id returned to every client correlates with nothing
description: grep 'slog.|log.' internal/transport returns ZERO hits. Neither http.Dependencies (http.go:76) nor mcp.Dependencies (mcp.go:78) has a Logger field and production.go:168-235 passes none. At http.go:246, mcp.go:791, http.go:262,267 the err variable is read once for a nil check and DROPPED. All 600 carefully-wrapped %w chains die silently at the boundary; the client gets 'INTERNAL: The request could not be completed.' newRequestID (mcp.go:974, http.go:463) mints req_<128 bits> per call and echoes it in every success and every ErrorDTO - and nothing logs it, so a user can paste you a request id that matches nothing. No inbound X-Request-Id is honored either. FIX: thread the logger already built at runtime.go:97 into both transport Dependencies; one Info access log per request keyed on request_id (operation, status/code, duration, actor) plus Error at the internalFailure sites; honor inbound X-Request-Id.

title: ValidateFence evaluates the fencing guarantee non-transactionally
description: operations.go:1560-1590 - the function deciding whether an agent still holds valid authority - runs ENTIRELY OUTSIDE a transaction on store.db. It issues loadLease (3 queries: :1601, :1616, :1639), then requireCurrentLeaseEpoch, then sqliteNow, then one query per fence: 6+ round trips each potentially on a DIFFERENT pooled connection, so there is no consistent snapshot. Another agent can acquire an overlapping exclusive lease and bump lease_fence_counters between the lease read and the counter read, and the lease's own expiry can pass mid-sequence. changeLease (:1500) does the equivalent checks correctly inside one withImmediate. This is the mechanism CLAUDE.md advertises as 'the fencing token doing its job'. FIX: wrap in BeginTx(ctx, &sql.TxOptions{ReadOnly:true}) - the driver issues a deferred BEGIN for read-only so it costs nothing.

title: AcquireLease full-scans the leases table inside the global write lock; expired leases are never reaped
description: operations.go:1387-1391 loads EVERY active lease selector in the workspace (EXPLAIN: SCAN lease); lease_selectors_overlap_idx (0002:69) is unused. Overlap is an O(requested x existing) nested loop in Go with an application.NewLeaseSelector parse allocated in the INNER loop (:1411). Expiry is only a filter (:1418), never a state transition - nothing sets status='released' except explicit release (:1529) and there is no reaper; offline.go:519 and admin.go:530 only REPORT expired-but-active leases. Every crashed agent leaves a row scanned forever. MEASURED: 5000 stale leases = 5.44ms per scan on top of the 5.12ms fsync, all holding the daemon-wide write lock. FIX: index leases(workspace_id, authority_epoch, status, expires_at_us) and filter expires_at_us > ? in SQL; add a reaper that flips expired active leases to released.

title: An empty inbox poll is a 33.9ms full scan and its cursor never advances
description: MEASURED at 100k messages/8 agents. EXPLAIN shows the inbox query (operations.go:1157-1173) drives off a rowid range scan of messages because position IS the rowid and satisfies ORDER BY for free; message_deliveries_inbox_idx (0002:43) is never used because it cannot supply position ordering. Timings: cursor=0 dense 0.30ms; cursor=99500 0.33ms; agent with NO matching mail 33.9ms. The last is the common case - agents poll and usually find nothing - and it is linear in repo-wide message count. Compounded by a cursor bug at operations.go:1230: 'next := after' is only overwritten when len(result) != 0, so an EMPTY PAGE RETURNS THE SAME CURSOR and a quiet agent re-scans the same growing distance forever. FIX: denormalize messages.position into message_deliveries and index (recipient_actor_id, position), partial on read_at_us IS NULL; advance the cursor on an empty page.

title: Acknowledging one message scans the entire inbox with an N+1 per page
description: findInboxMessageDigest (mcp.go:524-541) pages the caller's COMPLETE inbox from position 0, 256 at a time, until it finds one message - just to fetch a digest. Each page calls loadMessages (operations.go:1156) which materializes every message body (up to 262144 bytes per the CHECK in 0002) and issues one loadVisibleDeliveries query PER ROW (:1205) - 256 extra round trips per page. Acking message #10000 costs ~10000 SQL statements. messages is never deleted so this grows forever. The fix already exists and the OTHER transport already uses it: GetVisibleMessage (operations.go:1107), called by local.go:148. FIX: use GetVisibleMessage; batch deliveries with WHERE message_id IN (...). Note :1237 also queries on store.db outside any txn, so a page is assembled from up to 257 different snapshots.

title: Every tool call, including reads, pays a durable fsync write for a heartbeat
description: MEASURED. AuthenticateLocalAgent (operations.go:1971) runs in withImmediate (a BEGIN IMMEDIATE write txn) because it unconditionally updates the session heartbeat at :1997. It is the first statement of EVERY MCP tool (mcp.go:328,345,384,401,422,497,553,617) and the HTTP local API (local.go:364). Writes are globally serialized by the in-process arbiter (sqlite.go:701) held across the whole txn. Benchmarked 300 sequential commits: shipped config (synchronous=FULL + fullfsync) 5.12ms/commit = 195 commits/s; without fullfsync 0.10ms = 9994/s; synchronous=NORMAL 0.04ms = 27388/s. So inbox_fetch pays 5ms of durable-write latency before it reads anything and message_send pays it twice (~10ms floor). FIX: authenticate in a read-only txn (registration_token_digest is already UNIQUE-indexed) and coalesce last_seen_at_us to at most once per session per N seconds. Keep fullfsync for genuine state changes.

title: 19 MCP tools are permanently UNAUTHENTICATED: the context key is never written
description: internal/runtime/production.go:334 gates every W0/W1 tool on ctx.Value(verifiedIngressContextKey{}). That key is DECLARED at production.go:323 and written nowhere - grep returns exactly two hits (declaration + read) and there is not one context.WithValue in the non-test tree. Verified empirically against the live daemon: create_workspace, get_context, sync_events, start_session, start_run, join_run, activate_objective, plan_run_with_bindings, observe_work_ref, create_objective_and_work, installation_bootstrap all return UNAUTHENTICATED unconditionally. 10 of the 19 are ALSO hardwired to handler.unavailable() (production.go:392-421). FIX: stop registering these on the MCP transport until a client can present verified ingress - they keep their full HTTP surface. One line per tool in NewServer (mcp.go:124-190) behind a Dependencies flag. Saves ~29.6k tokens per request with zero capability loss.

title: localsecurity denials become retryable HTTP 500s and skip the denial audit
description: localsecurity/security.go:63 ErrAccessDenied is a plain errors.New, not a *domain.CommandError. orchestration.go:1310 only recognises the latter, so the denial-audit branch (:1317) is never reached and the sentinel lands at http.go:246 -> internalFailure: INTERNAL / retryable:true / recovery:retry_same_command. A permission denial instructs the agent to retry forever, at a 500, with no audit row. FIX: return domain.NewCommandError(ErrorCodeForbidden|ErrorCodeCapabilityRequired, reason, cause).

title: Lease conflict discards the holder, expiry and selector it is holding at that instant
description: internal/storage/sqlite/operations.go:1420 returns 'an active overlapping lease exists'. The query at :1388 already selected lease_id, mode, selector_path and expires_at_us, and loop var 'prior' holds all four at the return. holder_actor_id is in the table and not even selected. Retryable() is false, so the agent is told do-not-retry with no expiry to wait for and no counterparty - while CLAUDE.md:311 instructs it to 'coordinate through a conversation'. FIX: select holder_actor_id, interpolate path/holder/expiry into the message and the new evidence schema.

title: Coordination MCP tools return raw Go errors, bypassing ErrorDTO entirely
description: registerCoordinationTools/registerReservationTools (internal/transport/mcp/mcp.go:311-592) hand the raw Go error to the SDK (e.g. mcp.go:573 'return nil, reservationOutput{}, err'). The *domain.CommandError carrying code, category, conflict kind and retry posture is flattened to a bare string. Agents cannot branch on the error code for agent_register, message_send, or any reservation tool. The W0/W1 tools DO go through the contract layer - there are two error paths and the good one is not wired to the tools agents use all day. FIX: shared helper that mints a request id, maps err through domain.CommandError like writeLocalError does, logs it, returns a structured error.

title: LEASE_CONFLICT / LEASE_EXPIRED / FENCE_REJECTED are rejected by their own validator
description: contracts/outcomes.go:1175 - these three codes 'do not have a frozen W0 typed evidence schema', so ANY ErrorDTO carrying them fails Validate(), and checkedFailure (http.go:411) replaces it with internalFailure = HTTP 500. Twelve lines earlier STALE_VERSION is REQUIRED to carry expected_version and actual_version. ErrorDetailsDTO (outcomes.go:837) has no holder/path/expiry field. FIX: add lease evidence fields to ErrorDetailsDTO and give these codes a real requireAndAllow mask instead of an outright rejection.

title: Data safety and lifecycle: backup, migration, retention
description: Backup/Restore is fully implemented and has zero callers while doctor tells users to restore backups. The migration ladder has one hardcoded rung so a skipped version dead-ends permanently. The event journal is append-only by trigger with no retention story.

title: MCP surface: stop charging every agent 29.6k tokens for uncallable API
description: Measured against the live daemon: tools/list is 130,703 bytes / ~32,676 tokens = 16.3 percent of a 200k context, on every request forever. 90.6 percent of it is 19 identity/work-plane tools that are provably impossible to call. The working product is 4 tools and ~3k tokens.

title: Agent error contract: coordination failures must carry recovery evidence
description: Blackbird has a rigorous per-error-code evidence contract (contracts/outcomes.go validateCodeDetails) that tells an agent exactly how to recover. The three codes that ARE the product - LEASE_CONFLICT, LEASE_EXPIRED, FENCE_REJECTED - are explicitly excluded from it, and the MCP tools agents actually use bypass the contract layer entirely. Net effect: the coordination primitive is opaque to its only users.

title: The shipped plugin clients discard the problem+json body they are handed
description: packages/claude-plugin/server.mjs:88,146,151,176 throw 'Blackbird registration failed with HTTP <status>'; packages/opencode-plugin/src/index.ts:419 does the same. local.go:500-517 is the ONE place that translates a CommandError properly (writeLocalProblem with code and message) and both shipped clients throw it away and report a bare number. FIX: parse application/problem+json and surface code + message.

title: doctor misdiagnoses a dead daemon and status exits 0
description: adminclient.go:89-92 returns nil on a probe failure so state.Failure is never set (status.go:334) and doctor.go:234's failure case is dead; control falls to :238. Verified live against a dead daemon: 'x FAIL daemon.liveness daemon answered but storage is unavailable: ... connection refused / remedy: run blackbird doctor --deep and inspect database.schema'. The daemon did not answer and the remedy points at the database schema. Separately blackbird status with a dead daemon prints 'reachable no' and EXITS 0 (status.go:40-55 faults only under --require-running). FIX: have Health return the probe error; add a !Reachable case above the readiness case in daemonCheck.

title: doctor ignores three fields already computed and handed to it
description: main.go:253,276,300 populate Database.FileMode, Database.FreeBytes and Database.ExpiredActiveLeases. doctor.go:249-303 consults none. So doctor passes clean on a group-readable database, on a disk with 40MB free, and with hundreds of expired-but-unreleased leases blocking every agent. FIX: three checks costing zero extra I/O - disk.free (warn below ~1GB or 10x DB size), database.permissions (fail if not -rw-------), reservations.expired (warn past a threshold, remedy blackbird reservations --state=expired).

title: ~970 cyclomatic points are duplicated between the sqlite and postgres adapters
description: 110 identically-named functions across the two adapters with suspiciously paired complexity: 33/33, 32/32, 28/28, 27/27, 24/24, 23/23, 20/20, 19/19, 16/16, 14/14, 13/13. Verified by diff: aggregateRefFromParts (cc 33 both sides) is VERBATIM identical except the locals were renamed value,err -> v,e - and it has no database dependency at all. resolveAuthenticationState differs only in the tx type, the clock SQL and the ErrNoRows sentinel. Postgres is at 2.6 percent coverage, so ~970 points of this is untested duplication that will drift from the tested twin. FIX: move aggregateRefFromParts to domain/application outright; collapse the rest onto a shared algorithm over a narrow tx port.

title: Enable a cognitive-complexity ratchet; every complexity linter is disabled
description: cyclop, gocyclo, gocognit, maintidx, nestif, funlen, dupl and gocritic are all disabled in .golangci.yml. That is why the tail got here and why it will grow. MEASURED: 14830 cyclomatic points over 3266 functions, average 4.54 (healthy), 137 functions at cc>=20, 46 at cc>=30, 8 at cc>=50. FIX: enable gocognit - NOT gocyclo - at a threshold just above today's worst and ratchet down; cognitive is right because it does not punish the flat dispatch tables (lockedTransitionMatches is 59 cyclomatic / 11 cognitive; applyNamedProperty is 30/1) which are the wrong shape but not dangerous. Add dupl scoped to internal/storage.

title: The event journal grows ~490MB/year with no retention story
description: MEASURED: 200000 lease.renewed events with a realistic 267-byte payload = 102MB, 511 bytes/event including index. A conservative dogfooding profile (8 agents renewing every 60s, 8h/day, 250 days) is 960000 events ~ 490MB/year from lease renewals ALONE, per project, plus one message.available row per RECIPIENT per message (operations.go:1080) and one per read/ack. Six tables carry no_delete triggers that RAISE(ABORT) and grep 'DELETE FROM' over non-test Go returns nothing. gc is honest about this (gc.go:9-11,109) but the consequence is a multi-gigabyte file whose only remedy is deleting it and losing all history. DECIDE NOW while the schema is cheap to change: either drop the no_delete trigger on coordination_events and add gc --prune --older-than keeping retained_from honest for cursor validation (streamHead already returns retainedFrom, operations.go:601), or declare append-only a product invariant in README with the measured bytes/event and make doctor warn past a threshold.

title: No metrics surface of any kind
description: grep expvar|prometheus|pprof|otel returns nothing but a comment. No request count, error rate, latency, lease-contention counter, queue depth, slow-query log or DB growth series. /readyz (health.go:113) reports status/storage/schema_version/check_ms for the last probe - that is the entire runtime telemetry. A user cannot answer 'is it slow or is it my agent'. FIX: expvar behind the existing localSafety gate on the loopback listener - no dependency, near free - publishing requests by operation and outcome, lease acquire/conflict/expire, SSE connections and DB size. Render in blackbird status -v.

title: Log verbosity is restart-only, under a supervisor
description: Level resolves once at startup from --log-level (daemon.go:19) or BLACKBIRD_LOG_LEVEL (runtime.go:26,84), baked into slog.HandlerOptions{Level: level} at runtime.go:102. Neither is a slog.LevelVar so nothing can change it later. Turning on debug means editing a plist or unit, restarting, and reproducing - for an intermittent bug that is the whole investigation lost. FIX: LevelVar + PUT on the already-authenticated admin surface (admin.go:252) fronted by blackbird log-level debug.

title: MCP sessions are never reaped and there is no admission control
description: production.go:243 passes nil to mcpServer.HTTPHandler(nil). The SDK is explicit (mcp/streamable.go:166-172): 'If SessionTimeout is the zero value, idle sessions are never closed'; the reaper installs only under SessionTimeout>0 (:721). Sessions leave the map only on explicit DELETE or transport error (:688-694), so any crashed agent or killed terminal leaks a map entry and its goroutines for the daemon's lifetime - the normal case on a laptop. Alongside: no rate limiter, no semaphore, no max-in-flight, no http.TimeoutHandler. runtime.go:266-270 sets only ReadHeaderTimeout and IdleTimeout - no ReadTimeout, no WriteTimeout. The only per-request deadline is CLIENT-SUPPLIED AND UNBOUNDED (http.go:243, mcp.go:729); validateDeadline (decode.go:421) checks only non-zero and UTC, so a client can name the year 3000. FIX: SessionTimeout 30m; clamp the deadline to a server max; in-flight semaphore emitting the RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED code that already exists and is never produced.

title: No Go benchmarks or load tests exist anywhere in the repository
description: grep 'func Benchmark' over the whole module returns zero. grep for soak/loadtest/stress returns zero files. make test-stress repeats the correctness suite and measures nothing. Every number in this audit had to be produced from outside the repo, and the fsync, inbox-scan and lease-scan regressions would all ship silently. FIX: bench_test.go with BenchmarkCommitLatency, BenchmarkInboxEmptyPoll (10k/100k seeded), BenchmarkAcquireLeaseWithStaleLeases, plus a make bench target and a benchstat-gated CI job against a checked-in baseline - the same argument COVERAGE_FLOOR already won.

title: The coordination protocol is documented only where agents cannot read it
description: register -> reserve narrowly -> renew with current fences -> release -> one conversation per work item lives in this repo's CLAUDE.md. An agent connecting from any other project sees 31 tool descriptions and nothing else. For an agents-first product the protocol must be discoverable from the tool surface and the error responses alone. FIX: encode the protocol in tool descriptions and in a blackbird_get_started/protocol resource.

title: The shipped blackbird skill routes agents into guaranteed failure
description: ~/.claude/skills/blackbird/SKILL.md tells agents to use objectives/work/runs for durable multi-session missions. All five of those tools are permanently UNAUTHENTICATED. FIX: rewrite the skill around the 4-call loop that actually works.

title: outputSchema is 59 percent of the tool-list wire (~19.3k tokens) and is largely redundant
description: Measured: 77,204 of 130,661 bytes. get_context spends 6,425 of its 7,037 bytes on outputSchema. reservation_renew and reservation_release each re-emit the whole reservationOutput schema that reservation_acquire already emitted - three near-identical copies. FIX: drop outputSchema on coordination tools (structured content is self-describing and every result is echoed as text) or $ref the shared shapes.

title: The agent_token / registration_token rename trap is invisible in the schema
description: CLAUDE.md:294 documents it; the product does not. registerAgentInput.RegistrationToken (mcp.go:190) is the only field with a hint and it does not mention the rename; the 11 agent_token fields (mcp.go:201,213,252,269,282,292,298) carry no description at all. Measured failure: passing registration_token to agents_list yields 'unexpected additional properties ["registration_token"]' and never says the tool calls it agent_token. Every fresh agent burns one guaranteed failed call. FIX: jsonschema description on every agent_token field naming its source.

title: No escape hatch for a lease held by a dead agent
description: MaxLeaseTTL is 24h (application.go:6831). Expired leases correctly stop blocking (operations.go:1417). But within the TTL there is no break, no steal, no force-release and no admin path - 'reservations' is in the CLI inspect group only. An agent that is compacted and loses its lease id locks out every other agent for up to 24h and the only recourse is hand-editing SQLite. ExpiredActiveLeases is already counted in offline inspection. FIX: blackbird reservation release --force <id>, plus an MCP reservations_list so agents can see holders.

title: Registration failures use one string for two opposite remedies
description: operations.go:1929 and :1946 both return 'registration token is not valid' - the first for no-record-at-all (remedy: re-register WITHOUT a token), the second for a digest mismatch (remedy: use the right token). Same for :1973/:1992 'agent token is not valid'. This is what every coordination tool returns after a daemon restart and it never says to call blackbird_agent_register. FIX: distinguish the four cases and name the remedy in the message - the coordination path has no other channel.

title: CommandError has no Message(), so 85 precise domain messages never reach the client
description: domain/errors.go:235-283 exposes Code/Category/Retryable/ConflictKind/Unwrap but no Message(). contracts/commands.go:1339 therefore substitutes commandFailureMessage(code) - one of eleven generics. 40 exact transition messages and 41 commandReferenceConflict messages are replaced or, for STATE_CONFLICT, fall to default: (commands.go:1375) and become a 500. FIX: add Message() and use it as the DTO message when non-empty.

title: A database failure is reported to the agent as a stale fence
description: operations.go:1584: 'if err := ...Scan(&current); err != nil || current != fence.Counter()' collapses a busy/locked timeout, an I/O error and a missing row into 'lease fence has been superseded'. The agent re-acquires and redoes work for a reason that never happened while the real failure stays invisible. FIX: split the condition - return the DB error or DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE separately from the counter mismatch.

title: Six fence-rejection sites report neither expected nor supplied fence
description: operations.go:1509,1515,1526,1569,1585,1863. Both sides of every comparison are in scope. equalFences (:1666) returns a bare bool and discards which key diverged. An agent told 'lease fence is stale' cannot tell whether it sent the wrong counter, the wrong key, or has a rotated epoch - three different remedies. Its lease is then unrenewable AND unreleasable until TTL expiry, which CLAUDE.md:305 calls the thing agents must avoid. FIX: make equalFences return the first divergence; report conflict key + expected + supplied.

title: Doctor and status: close the diagnostic gaps
description: doctor is the best-designed surface in the repo and has cheap, high-value gaps: it ignores three fields already computed for it, never verifies the MCP client registration that IS the delivery model, misdiagnoses a dead daemon, and has no opinion on fields status displays.

title: Complexity and coverage: finish the tail
description: 14,830 cyclomatic points over 3,266 functions; average 4.54 is healthy, the tail is not. 137 functions at cc>=20, 8 at cc>=50. The worst (authorize, cc 93 / cognitive 72) sits at 0.0 percent coverage. No complexity linter is enabled. ~970 cc points are duplicated between the sqlite and postgres adapters.

title: Observability: give the daemon a voice
description: slog appears in 3 files, all under internal/runtime. Nothing in transport, storage, application, or integration logs anything. A request_id is minted and returned to every client and written to no log. 600 carefully-wrapped error chains die silently at the transport boundary.

title: Silently swallowed errors that hide real failures
description: (1) operations.go:2101-2108 coordinationError/coordinationConflict do 'result, _ := domain.NewCommandError(...)'. On construction failure this returns a TYPED-NIL *CommandError in a non-nil interface: errors.As succeeds, Code() is empty, statusFor('') is 500, Error() prints literally <nil>. Not reachable today; the _ guarantees it never will be caught. (2) adminclient.go:79-80 drops the discovery error whenever an address was salvaged, so a corrupt handshake silently probes the wrong address. (3) production.go:319 'defer func(){ _ = registry.Revoke(request) }()' - a failed revoke leaks a live registration with nothing logged. (4) install.go:918 '_, _ = Runner.Run(ctx, launchctl, bootout, ...)' inside restart - a genuine bootout failure means bootstrap runs against a still-loaded service and install reports success while the old daemon keeps running. (5) sqlite.go:598 and :642 collapse an 11-clause and a 9-clause boolean OR into one message with every compared value in a local variable - a daemon-wont-start error with no indication which invariant failed.

title: Remedy strings exist in two incompatible types and are barely used
description: FaultError.Remedy (cli/errors.go:51, set via withRemedy :71) is printed at cli.go:327 and emitted as JSON at errors.go:164 - but has only 7 call sites. The parallel checkResult.Remedy (doctor.go:27, 7 good strings) is referenced nowhere outside doctor.go. Nothing equivalent exists daemon-side: ErrorDetailsDTO carries a Recovery ENUM but no human remedy string, so an MCP agent never gets prose telling it what to do. FIX: merge the two remedy types; add a remedy string to ErrorDetailsDTO from the same table.

title: status prints clean-shutdown with no explanation and doctor has no opinion on it
description: status.go:229 renders 'clean-shutdown no' while the daemon is running (semantically correct - the DB is open) and doctor reports 8 passed 0 warned. A user reads that as alarming, checks doctor, is told everything is fine, and learns that status output does not mean anything. INVARIANT WORTH ADOPTING: doctor has an opinion about everything status displays. FIX: explain it inline or have doctor speak to it.

title: Coverage floor has 2.1 points of slack
description: MEASURED 67.1 percent against COVERAGE_FLOOR 65.0. Postgres 2.6 percent, localsecurity 67.0, application 70.5. Uncovered-complexity by package (cc>=10 weighted by 1-coverage): application 857/3081, postgres 692/716, sqlite 401/1262, contracts 272/990. Note the refactor direction is coverage-POSITIVE - deleting untested postgres clones removes uncovered statements and testing authorize adds covered ones - so ratchet COVERAGE_FLOOR in Makefile AND the CI workflow together as slack grows.

title: WAL grows unchecked; the only remedy requires stopping the daemon
description: Observed live: 663.9 KiB WAL against a 4 KiB database (166x) with doctor reporting 8 passed 0 warned. Nothing checkpoints while the daemon runs and gc --checkpoint/--vacuum both require a stopped daemon (gc.go) - for a background service the user installed and forgot. FIX: opportunistic PASSIVE checkpoint on an idle timer; a WAL-size check in doctor.

title: Daemon logs grow without bound; no rotation
description: The launchd plist appends to blackbird.log/blackbird.err.log forever (install.go:1105) with no rotation, truncation or size cap anywhere. logsource.go:26 caps only the READ window at 512KB. FIX: rotate at a size cap on daemon boot.

title: No support-bundle command
description: No support-bundle or debug dump in the grammar (cli.go:39-59). Filing a useful bug means six commands and judgment from a user who by definition does not know what matters. FIX: blackbird support-bundle [--out] emitting version, OS/arch, doctor --deep --json, status --json, gc --json, both log tails, install paths and service definition, and the detected MCP client entries. MUST redact the admin token from the handshake record and service definition.

title: Connection pool is hardcoded at 5 with no knob
description: maximumReadPoolSize = 5 (sqlite.go:38) drives SetMaxOpenConns/SetMaxIdleConns (:144) with no config and no env override. Writes serialize above SQLite so this is a genuine read-concurrency cap of 5 daemon-wide. With the 33.9ms empty inbox poll that is ~150 empty polls/sec at 100k messages, with every SSE stream competing for the same 5 slots and requests queueing invisibly inside database/sql with no metric. FIX: Config field defaulted from runtime.NumCPU(). Preserve verifyPhysicalConnections (sqlite.go:604) which checks pragmas on all pooled connections and is genuinely excellent.

title: Shutdown has no drain barrier; one SSE client forces the full 30s and an unclean marker
description: runtime.go:483-514 orders shutdown correctly but nothing enforces it: http.Server.Shutdown returns ctx.Err() at the 30s stopCtx (:487) and the loop proceeds to close the store while handlers still run. No WaitGroup over handlers, no fallback Server.Close(). Reachable normally: Shutdown does not cancel request contexts and the SSE handler (local.go:263) blocks until the client disconnects, so one connected agent makes every shutdown take 30s and then closes the store under a live SyncCoordinationEvents. Store.Close (sqlite.go:1401) then has only 5s to write its clean-shutdown marker, so a contended shutdown can mark the database unclean. FIX: cancellable runtime-owned context for SSE and MCP handlers, cancelled at shutdown start, with a WaitGroup that store.Close waits on.

title: outbox_jobs is written and never drained; ANALYZE is never run
description: insertOutboxEffects (command.go:1164-1180) writes outbox_jobs rows with status='pending'. Grep across non-test non-Postgres Go finds ONLY those writes - no dispatcher, no status update, no reaper. Rows accumulate as permanently pending work with a full payload BLOB each, and outbox_jobs_ready_idx (0001:594) indexes a queue nothing drains. Separately grep for ANALYZE / PRAGMA optimize / sqlite_stat returns nothing, so the planner runs on built-in defaults for the life of the database and the gap widens as tables grow. FIX: wire a dispatcher or stop writing the table; run PRAGMA optimize on Close and periodically.

title: Performance and scale: the daemon has a 195 call/sec ceiling and no benchmarks
description: Measured on this machine against the shipped DSN. Every MCP tool call including read-only ones performs a durable F_FULLFSYNC write, capping the whole daemon at ~195 calls/sec. An empty inbox poll is a 33.9ms full scan whose cursor never advances. AcquireLease full-scans a table that is never reaped. There is not one Go benchmark in the repository, so all three would regress silently.

title: Twelve coordination tools could be seven
description: message_mark_read and message_acknowledge literally share a handler (registerDeliveryFactTool, mcp.go:490) - collapse to message_fact{kind}. message_send/message_reply differ by one optional field (mcp.go:227). reservation_renew/reservation_release differ by one bool (mcp.go:635). Fewer choices, fewer tokens, less ambiguity.

title: W0/W1 input schemas are unsatisfiable by a language model
description: blackbird_start_session requires 13 top-level fields including pattern-constrained UUIDv7 command_id/authority_id/authority_epoch/correlation_id plus 8 required optimistic-concurrency integers, with no tool to obtain any of them. 'schema' and 'operation' are bare strings with no const/enum/description. 40 properties, zero descriptions. This is an internal RPC envelope leaked verbatim into an agent-facing API (mcp.go:694-700).

title: Only 4 parameter descriptions exist across 31 input schemas; one enum is prose
description: topic, subject, body, to, lease_id, fences, conflict_key, counter, message_id, conversation_id, after, unread_only are all bare types. Selector kind is jsonschema:'exact or subtree' (mcp.go:278) - prose, not an enum - so kind:'file' passes the validator and is rejected opaquely by the handler. 'to' takes agent NAMES and nothing says so. Nothing documents exact vs subtree, mark_read vs acknowledge, or inbox_fetch vs thread_fetch. FIX: real enums + descriptions.

title: 19 of 31 tool descriptions are byte-identical boilerplate
description: mcp.go:708 emits operation + '; authorized, bounded, idempotent command/query with strict versioned input.' This restates the name, describes the transport rather than the effect, and gives an agent choosing between siblings nothing. Conditional on the tools surviving the gating decision.

title: 'invalid coordination contract' is one opaque message for at least three unrelated mistakes
description: Measured: bad lease_id uuid, selector kind 'file', and an out-of-range fence counter all return 'invalid coordination contract' (mcp.go:405,443,455,631 -> application.ErrInvalidCoordination). The SDK's own generated validator is strictly better: mode:'write' yields 'enum: write does not equal any of: [shared exclusive]'. FIX: distinct messages naming the field and the accepted form.
